title: transaction.created payload, v1
description:
Published on `transaction.created.v1` when a transaction has been accepted and durably persisted. Emitted through the transactional outbox, so its existence means the row was committed - not that it is about to be.

Keyed by ACCOUNT id, not transaction id (ADR-0006): Kafka orders only within a partition, and velocity rules need one account's transactions in order.

The envelope's `aggregateId` is the transaction id; `accountId` here is the partition key.

accountId.description: The partition key for this topic. Present in the payload as well as the Kafka key so a consumer reading a record in isolation - from a DLQ, or from a console dump - still knows which account it belongs to.

deviceReference.description: Synthetic device handle, or null where the channel has no device. Null rather than absent so a consumer never distinguishes 'no device' from 'field missing'.

occurredAt.description: When the transaction took place. Distinct from the envelope's occurredAt only in replay, where a historical transaction is ingested now.

ingestionSource.description: How this transaction entered the system. `SCENARIO_REPLAY` is what tells a consumer the data is a rerun of a known scenario rather than live synthetic traffic.

idempotencyKey.description: The client-supplied key this transaction was accepted under, unique per account. Carried so a consumer can correlate back to the original submission.
